one_liner: Zero-copy shared-memory publish/subscribe IPC for C++ and C; sub-microsecond same-host latency versus POSIX message queues and Unix sockets.
what_it_does: iceoryx is an inter-process communication middleware: publishers and subscribers on one host exchange samples through shared-memory pools managed by a central daemon (iox-roudi). The API is not a socket replacement: a publisher loans a chunk from shared memory, writes into it in place and publishes it, and the subscriber takes and later releases that chunk. It offers typed and untyped C++ APIs, a C binding, WaitSet/Listener for event-driven receive, and request/response (client/server) in addition to pub/sub.
how_it_is_fast: True zero-copy: the payload is written once into a pre-allocated shared-memory chunk and only a chunk reference (iceoryx's RelativePointer, valid in every process's mapping) travels through lock-free shared-memory queues (hoofs SpscSofi / MpmcLockfreeQueue) to each subscriber, so per-message cost does not grow with payload size. Chunks come from fixed-size mempools configured at RouDi start-up (for example 128 B to 4 MB) and are handed out by a lock-free free list (MpmcLoFFLi), so a polling receiver's hot path has no kernel copy, no syscall and no heap allocation; event-driven receivers can block on a WaitSet or Listener instead.
when_to_use: Moving large messages (camera frames, point clouds, tensors from hundreds of kB to MB) between processes on the same machine, where a socket or message queue would copy the payload through the kernel on every hop.
Robotics and automotive stacks already on ROS 2 (rmw_iceoryx), Cyclone DDS shared-memory transport, eCAL or AUTOSAR Adaptive bindings that build on iceoryx.
Latency-sensitive one-to-many pub/sub on Linux or QNX where you can dedicate a polling core or accept WaitSet wake-up cost, and payload sizes are bounded and known up front.
Existing iceoryx deployments that need a stable, security-patched C++ IPC layer while planning a move to iceoryx2.
when_not_to_use: New projects: the README says iceoryx classic is in maintenance mode (security fixes only, no further major releases) and will reach end of life shortly after iceoryx2 v1.0; the maintainers recommend iceoryx2.
Communication across machines: there is no network transport; remote traffic needs a gateway such as iceoryx-gateway-dds.
Small, infrequent messages where a Unix socket's few microseconds do not matter: you pay for a daemon, shared-memory sizing (/dev/shm, Docker --shm-size) and a loan/release API discipline.

Untrusted peers: all participants map the same shared-memory segments; open bug reports include possible double free of chunks (#562), mutex-owner-died chunk locking errors (#2193) and RouDi or Listener deadlock risks (#1546, #1711, #2202).

Unbounded or highly variable payload sizes: a loan larger than the biggest configured mempool fails, and exhausting a pool yields MEPOO__MEMPOOL_GETCHUNK_POOL_IS_RUNNING_OUT_OF_CHUNKS unless you resize the RouDi config.

integration.dependencies: iox-roudi daemon at run time; libacl (Linux and QNX); optional cpptoml for TOML RouDi config and ncurses for the introspection tool; built with CMake 3.16+ (Bazel build also offered)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17-era hoofs (README describes STL constructs beyond C++17); GCC 8.3+, Clang 9+, MSVC 2019+, CMake 3.16+
integration.platforms: Linux and QNX (full feature set, shared-memory access rights), macOS, FreeBSD and Windows 10 (no shared-memory access rights); 64-bit for production, 32-bit is a technology preview
integration.thread_safety: not documented as a blanket guarantee; publishers and subscribers are per-process endpoints, RouDi and the WaitSet/Listener are designed for concurrent processes
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: a different API (loan/publish/take/release with a central daemon) replaces mq_send/sendto; the protocol shape (one-way pub/sub or request/response on one host) is the same

gotchas: The README benchmark table is old: the same Xeon E3-1505M v5 output appears in the v0.90.0 README (apps then named iceperf-laurel/hardy) and was never regenerated; the current harness also runs 16 B to 512 B payloads and an iceoryx WaitSet (blocking receive) variant, neither of which has published numbers.

Harness flaw behind the large-payload ratios: the message-queue and Unix-socket baselines are capped at 4 kB per message (2 kB for the socket on macOS) and, for bigger payloads, send the same first 4 kB slice of the buffer subPackets times into a single 4 kB receive buffer; the 4096 kB rows are therefore 1024 cache-hot syscall pairs, not a 4 MB copy, while iceoryx never writes or reads beyond the 12-byte header. The 2,000x-2,800x figures measure syscall count, not data movement.

Every transport busy-polls (nonblocking mq_receive/recvfrom loops, iceoryx take() loop), and only a single average per size is printed (no percentiles, one run); blocking wake-up latency, which dominates real event-driven receivers, is not in the published data.

In the iceperf iceoryx path, a failed loan (payload larger than the largest mempool, or pool exhausted) silently sends nothing, so the leader spins forever rather than reporting an error; size the RouDi mempools (iceperf ships iceperf-roudi with pools up to 4 MB) before benchmarking.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (eRPC, Homa, Machnet, brpc, DRPC and the gRPC alternatives) all move bytes over a network stack; pick iceoryx only when both endpoints share one host and payloads are large, where passing a shared-memory pointer beats any socket-based RPC. For cross-machine RPC, eRPC (kernel bypass) or brpc remain the relevant choices.
verified_claims_summary: First-party iceperf example output on a Xeon E3-1505M v5 under Ubuntu 18.04 (compiler and flags not stated, single run, 100,000 round trips, one-way latency taken as half the round trip): iceoryx about 0.6-0.73 us at every payload from 1 kB to 4096 kB versus 3.1 us (message queue) and 4.3 us (Unix domain socket) at 1 kB, about 4x and 6x. The 4096 kB ratios (1.2e+03 and 1.7e+03 us, about 2,000x and 2,800x) come from baselines fragmenting into 1024 repeated 4 kB sends while iceoryx passes a pointer and never touches the payload.
status_note: Apache-2.0, 2.2k stars and widely integrated (ROS 2, Cyclone DDS, eCAL, AUTOSAR stacks), latest release v2.0.8, but iceoryx classic is in maintenance mode with security fixes only and end of life planned shortly after iceoryx2 v1.0, so use it for existing integrations and evaluate iceoryx2 for new work.
